inputs.source: Published HR policy documents returned by policy_search, authored by the HR content team under two-person publish review

instructions.note: The restriction against giving legal advice is enforced only by a prompt instruction with no structural backstop (such as an output classifier). Consequence is limited because the agent has no capability beyond reading the published policy index and replying to the asking employee.

controls.name: Least-privilege read-only credential scoped to the policy index
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by the credential/IAM layer outside the model. A more capable or manipulated model cannot gain write access or reach other systems without a separate credential grant.

controls.name: Network egress denied by default, verified by penetration test
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced at the network layer outside the model and verified by a pen test. The model has no code path to open a new network connection, so this does not decay with capability.

controls.name: Chat client does not render images or auto-fetch links
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by the client application, not the model. Closes the rendered-link or image side channel regardless of what text the model is induced to output.

controls.name: Two-person review required to publish policy content
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by the HR publishing workflow outside the model, so model capability does not change whether two humans reviewed the content. It narrows, rather than eliminates, the chance that embedded instructions or errors pass review.

controls.name: Prompt instruction: do not give legal advice
controls.decay_rationale: Relies on the model choosing to follow the instruction. A more capable or manipulated model can reason its way to an exception.

controls.name: Prompt instruction: use policy_search and quote the policy
controls.decay_rationale: Relies on model compliance; a hijacked or more capable model could answer without quoting the retrieved text, or quote it selectively or out of context.

controls.name: Model version pinned; upgrade requires a change ticket
controls.decay_rationale: Change control enforced outside the model. Prevents a silent, unreviewed model_upgrade trigger, though a reviewed upgrade can still later weaken the dependent prompt controls.

controls.name: Automated scan of newly published policy content for embedded model-directed instructions
controls.decay_rationale: Would be enforced in the publishing pipeline outside the model, as a second structural layer alongside human review, independent of model capability.

findings.title: Indirect injection or poisoning via the published policy index reaching the employee reply

forecast.watch_signal: Model version string changes in config without a corresponding control re-review, or the two-person publish review step is skipped or bypassed (for example, an emergency single-approver publish).

evidence.observation: The policy index holds only published policies; only the HR content team can write to it, and publishing requires two person review.
The agent is instructed to use policy_search to find the relevant policy and quote it, so retrieved document text is inserted directly into the model's context and output.
policy_search.search takes a free-text query and returns index content; nothing in the manifest indicates output sanitization or content provenance tagging.

recommendations.action: Add automated scanning of newly published policy content for embedded model-directed instructions or suspicious markup before it enters the search index, alongside the existing two-person review.
Periodically sample agent replies that quote policy content for unexpected directives, legal-advice language, or claims inconsistent with the source policy, to catch poisoning or drift early.

findings.title: Intended Q&A flow: authenticated employee question answered from the published policy index

forecast.watch_signal: No material change expected from these triggers alone on this path; re-assess if the agent gains a new egress channel, broader data scope, or a write/execute capability.

evidence.observation: The agent answers only questions about published Acme HR policies using policy_search, and tells the user when the policy does not answer plus links the HR portal.
Replies go only to the authenticated requester's own chat session; the agent has no other tools, no memory, and no network egress.

rating.rationale: The core Q&A flow (a trusted employee question leading to an internal read and an internal reply bound to the requester's own authenticated session) is low risk by design: no network egress, a least-privilege read-only credential, and no rendering of links or images. The one inherent-moderate finding is indirect injection or poisoning via the published policy pipeline, which is internal rather than untrusted content, reaching the employee reply. Two-person publish review plus the least-privilege credential bring this to a residual of low today, and the network-egress-deny and no-render-client structural controls close off exfiltration paths regardless of model capability. The forecast returns to moderate only if a model upgrade defeats the behavioral prompt instructions at the same time the two-person review step is bypassed or removed, since those are the only controls currently narrowing that path.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts (system prompt, tool manifest, runtime notes), not observed runtime behavior; aside from the stated network pen test, production behavior was not independently tested.

Autonomy step and runtime limits (max_unattended_steps, max_runtime_minutes) were not explicitly stated in the artifacts; the values used were inferred from the single-tool, synchronous Q&A design described. Confirming explicit runtime caps would raise confidence.
No MCP configuration or IaC was provided; capability scope for policy_search is inferred from tools.json and the runtime notes, so confidence on capability scope is medium.
The adequacy of the two-person publish review process (for example, whether reviewers are trained to catch embedded instructions) was not verified; its effectiveness is taken as declared.
